note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for persistent PSA elevation despite prior negative biopsy results.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer screening with fluctuating PSA levels. Patient is a 68-year-old secondary school teacher, married, living with partner. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with IPSS score of 1/35. He is a current smoker with 24 pack-years and consumes 29 units of alcohol weekly. He cycles 3 times per week for approximately 30 km. He has a history of hypercholesterolaemia and obesity. He takes atorvastatin, simvastatin, and rosuvastatin. He has a mild allergy to iodinated contrast. His daughter manages communication and is copied on letters with his consent.

On DRE, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged without nodules or asymmetry, consistent with cT1c. General examination shows no lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses. Vital signs are stable with BP 129/78 mmHg and HR 64 bpm.

next_of_kin: None recorded — patient declines to nominate
